title: A safety claim is an attribution claim
subtitle: The cost you are quoted is usually not the check, and the guarantee you assume is watching the wrong resource
framing: **ver_C refutes a belief and names it on page one: that a safety number is a fact about safety.** It is an attribution claim, and this corpus misassigns both halves. On the cost side, of the ten comparable safe-tuned-minus-unsafe rows above 100 instructions per call, a bounds check is the named dominant term on **three** — and the same three survive every threshold from 50 to 300, signed or absolute, so the cut-off is not doing the work. On five the mechanism is something else entirely; one has no attribution anywhere in the tree and is reported as unattributed; on the tenth the cost *is* the check, and one provably dead line deletes the whole per-pop term, leaving a five-instruction constant nobody has tried to remove. **The method that follows is one sentence — remove the mechanism and re-measure — and it caught an error before publication**, on a refused row that would have reported safe Rust 6.02× cheaper with 108.4% of the gap in the allocator and the check at 3% of the magnitude, opposite in sign. On the coverage side the answer is not one answer, and that is the finding: four detectors return the same verdict on **five of the ten rows where all four are measured**, silent together where the defect never leaves the allocation they watch — but silent together on timing for a different reason, because there they range over values while a leak is a property of the trace. One word, two answers, which is the only vocabulary this version coins. And one silence in that table is neither: a sanitizer owned the exact check for the exact defect and a **hardening flag** took the call off its path, so the one true blind spot was made by a second safety mechanism. ver_C is therefore a paper about **attribution and measurement**, in which C and Rust are the instrument rather than the subject — which is *why* it is useful to someone deciding on a rewrite. It keeps ver_B's readability and ver_A's willingness to argue, files every limitation beside the claim it bounds instead of in a section of its own, and runs its spine on one kernel redrawn rather than ten cited. It also retracts a claim of its own predecessor's: ver_B's detector table asserted that no cell reads *silent, and it should have seen this*, and that was true only after six of twelve rows had been dropped — one of them the row whose sanitizer was blinded. Restoring the table costs this version its more quotable number and it prints the smaller one.
